tags.name: Adam Jones
tags.description: Adam Thomas Jones, born January 15, 1965, is a multifaceted American artist renowned as the lead guitarist for the progressive metal band Tool. His musical prowess has earned him accolades, including being ranked 75th-greatest guitarist by Rolling Stone and 9th in Guitar World’s Top 100 Greatest Metal Guitarists. Jones’s signature sound is crafted using a 1979 Gibson Les Paul Custom Silverburst , often played through a Diezel VH4 amplifier. His pedalboard typically includes a Boss DD-3 Digital Delay, MXR Micro Amp, and a Boss BF-2 Flanger, contributing to Tool’s distinctive, atmospheric tone. Beyond music, Jones is also an accomplished animator and visual artist, having worked on films like Jurassic Park before focusing on Tool . His creative vision extends to the band’s music videos and live visuals, showcasing his diverse artistic talents.

tags.name: Fender Guitars & Gear
tags.description: Your ultimate guide to Fender guitars – from the Fender Stratocaster to the Telecaster, Jaguar, and Mustang, as well as everything else in between. Here’s all the latest Fender news, reviews, and user guides… To say that Fender is iconic would be the understatement of the century. Fender guitars have been used by the greats for over half a century now, and the company is still going strong with huge demand for its classic models like the Fender Stratocaster, Telecaster, Jazz, and Mustang . Next to Gibson , Fender was one of the first electric guitar companies. You cannot talk about the history of the guitar without talking about Leo Fender. Similarly, some of the most iconic music ever committed to tape was recorded using Fender guitars – and that still stands today. Which famous guitarists played Fender? Quite a few – Ritchie Blackmore, Jeff Beck, Eric Clapton, David Gilmore, Kurt Cobain, George Harrison, Hendrix, and Buddy Holly . In more recent years, you have players like Jim Root of Slipknot, Brant Bjork, and Rage Against The Machine’s Tom Morello. And, yes, you can use Fender guitars for metal music . Fender is so popular and has been for decades that most people cannot think about a guitar without thinking about a Fender. The Fender Stratocaster , for instance, has been one of the best-selling electric guitars since the 1960s. And in 2021, it is still flying off the shelves at music stores the globe over.

tags.name: Gibson Guitars
tags.description: The ultimate guide to Gibson guitars — from the Gibson Les Paul, SG, Explorer, and ES. We cover all of Gibson’s most iconic models, guitarists that used them, as well as all the latest news and reviews When it comes to iconic guitars, there are two names that everybody knows: Gibson and Fender. The reason for this is simple too: Gibson and Fender basically invented the modern electric guitar , way back in the 1950s. The most iconic of all Gibson guitars is, of course, the Gibson Les Paul. But like Fender, Gibson isn’t a one-trick pony – it has other, extremely popular guitar models like its Gibson SG, the Gibson Flying V, The Gibson ES, and the Gibson Explorer to name just a few of Gibson’s most iconic guitar lines. Favored by famous guitarists like Jimmy Page, Tony Iommi, Buzz Osbourne, Adam Jones , and a raft of other players dating back to the 1960s, the Gibson Les Paul is just about as iconic as it gets. Les Paul and Fender’s Strat are the two most well-known and loved guitars of all time. Like Fender , Gibson has been popular since the 1950s. In this time, everybody from metal acts to pop music players has used its guitars to craft some of the best records ever committed to tape. Gibson now makes a plethora of models, custom shop editions, and various configurations of its popular SG, Les Paul , and ES models.

tags.name: Music Theory
tags.description: What is Music Theory? Usually, when most beginner players think about music theory, they panic – you think of maths, of school, that it’ll be boring. But this couldn’t be farther from the truth. Sure, it is a task learning something new but with an understanding of music theory under your belt, even a basic one, you’ll see massive gains in your understanding of the guitar. Many players avoid music theory when starting out with guitar, but this is a mistake. The faster you understand how the guitar works, how its fretboard flows, and how notes and scales go together, the quicker you can start working on creating your own music. And keep in mind, that most iconic, classic music is incredibly simple – some songs are just two chords . The music theory guides for guitar below will open up realms of new possibilities for you as a guitarist. You’ll learn how scales work, how chord progressions work, and how guitar chords are made. And once you understand this, you can start creating and writing your own music and riffs. Learning music theory for the guitar is one of the best things a beginner or experienced guitarist can do, so do yourself a favor and start the process TODAY…
